projects.title: API-Based Data Pipeline & Feature Engineering System
projects.description: - Designed scalable API-driven data pipelines to collect, clean, and process large datasets- Engineered high-dimensional feature sets (100+ features) for classification and modeling tasks- Built end-to-end workflows for data ingestion, preprocessing, and model integration- Optimized pipeline efficiency for handling noisy and heterogeneous data sources

projects.title: Autonomous Robotics Localization & Navigation
projects.description: - Developed a 1D Particle Filter for robot localization, utilizing RK4 (Runge-Kutta) integration to improve odometry accuracy.- Implemented a weighting and resampling algorithm to handle sensor noise, allowing the robot to maintain a precise state estimate in dynamic environments.- Applied Inverse and Forward Kinematics for prismatic and revolute robot arms to enable precise path planning and obstacle avoidance.

projects.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Machine Learning Model
projects.description: - Built a hybrid quantum-classical model using PyTorch and PennyLane for binary classification on high-dimensional molecular datasets- Designed and integrated variational quantum circuits (VQCs) with classical layers for end-to-end training- Implemented Quantum State Regression (QSR) to improve adversarial robustness and model stability- Benchmarked performance against classical baselines, analyzing tradeoffs in accuracy and robustness

projects.title: Real-Time Operating System (RTOS) Kernel Development
projects.description: - Engineered a custom multitasking kernel for the ARM Cortex-M4 processor using ARMv7 Thumb2 assembly and C.- Implemented a robust system call (SVC) handler and dispatcher to manage privileged hardware access and process synchronization primitives.- Developed a Rate Monotonic Scheduler (RMS) to ensure deterministic execution for time-critical tasks.- Managed low-level interrupt priorities and context switching to maintain system stability under high-concurrency loads.

projects.title: Robotics Simulation & Trajectory Optimization
projects.description: - Developed simulation environments to study robot locomotion and control strategies- Analyzed the impact of mechanical design (e.g., spine structures) on system performance- Implemented trajectory optimization techniques under varying constraints- Evaluated tradeoffs between hardware design and control policies in robotic systems

activity.title: Congratulations! Rooting for you guys. Shreenabh Agrawal and Jaskaran Singh Walia

OpenRelay (YC S26) provides one API for inference across every chip. OpenRelay gives developers a single entry point for inference across every accelerator. You send a workload; OpenRelay schedules it onto the best-fit chip - NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium, or TPU - across clouds and hands back one production endpoint, typically 20% cheaper than renting the hardware yourself. You never pick the chip, chase quotas, or rebuild your stack per provider. It works in both directions: operators with idle accelerators can connect capacity to OpenRelay’s rails and get inference demand without building a platform themselves. The company is live in production, running 100 billion tokens a week across 22 locations on four continents and 11 accelerator SKUs. Jaden Wang built a half-megawatt data center and built virtualization at Voltage Park. Prashant Patel developed accelerator infrastructure at AWS, writing custom kernels for Trainium. They saw the same gap from opposite sides: there’s more AI compute than ever, and you still can’t reach it. Congrats on the launch, Jaden and Prashant! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gSAqpV6U
We launched on YC 🚀 If you’re working with robot automation or CNC machines, check out the video. Cheers to our amazing team behind this technology Robin Lee, Lucas Kover Wolf , Kamya Singh .
